questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is tissue respiration?

(ii) Describe how anaerobes break down glucose in cells. *[10 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Tissue respiration** *(3 marks)*

**Tissue (cellular or internal) respiration** is the **controlled, stepwise oxidation of organic molecules, mainly glucose, inside living cells** (in the cytoplasm and mitochondria) to **release energy**, which is used to make **ATP**. It differs from breathing (external respiration), which is only gas exchange. In aerobic conditions:

$$\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6\,O_2 \rightarrow 6\,CO_2 + 6\,H_2O + energy}$$

**(ii) How anaerobes break down glucose** *(7 marks)*

Anaerobes break down glucose **without oxygen** by **glycolysis followed by fermentation**; the glucose is only partly broken down. All the steps occur in the **cytoplasm**.

1. **Glycolysis.** Glucose (6C) is **phosphorylated** using **2 ATP** and split into **two triose phosphate** molecules (3C). These are **oxidised** (hydrogen is removed and taken by **NAD** to form **reduced NAD**) and converted to **two molecules of pyruvate**. **4 ATP** are made, so the **net gain is 2 ATP** per glucose.
2. **Regeneration of NAD.** Without oxygen, the reduced NAD cannot be reoxidised by the electron transport chain, so **pyruvate is used as the hydrogen acceptor**. This regenerates NAD so that glycolysis can continue.
   - **Alcoholic fermentation (yeast, some plant tissues).** Pyruvate is **decarboxylated** to **ethanal** (releasing $\mathrm{CO_2}$), and ethanal is **reduced to ethanol** by reduced NAD:

   $$\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2\,C_2H_5OH + 2\,CO_2 + 2\,ATP}$$

   - **Lactic acid fermentation (many bacteria, and mammalian muscle in a lack of oxygen).** Pyruvate is **reduced directly to lactate** (lactic acid), catalysed by lactate dehydrogenase:

   $$\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2\,CH_3CHOHCOOH + 2\,ATP}$$

3. The end products (ethanol, lactate) still **contain much chemical energy**, so only a small part of the energy of glucose is released (about 118 kJ per mole of glucose in alcoholic fermentation, against about 2870 kJ in complete oxidation). Some bacteria give other end products, such as ethanoic, propionic or butanoic acid.

questions.enonce_markdown: Differentiate between aerobic and anaerobic respiration. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Feature | Aerobic respiration | Anaerobic respiration |
|---|---|---|
| **Oxygen** | **Needs free oxygen** as the final electron acceptor | **No oxygen needed** |
| **Site in the cell** | Glycolysis in the **cytoplasm**; link reaction, Krebs cycle in the **mitochondrial matrix**; electron transport chain on the **cristae** | **Entirely in the cytoplasm** |
| **Breakdown of glucose** | **Complete** oxidation to $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O}$ | **Incomplete**: ethanol and $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (yeast), or lactate (muscle, bacteria) |
| **Energy yield** | **High**: about 2870 kJ per mole of glucose, about **30 to 32 ATP** | **Low**: about 118 kJ per mole in yeast (**2 ATP** net) |
| **End products** | Carbon dioxide and water, which are harmless | Ethanol or lactic acid, which are **toxic** in large amounts and still contain energy |
| **Where it occurs** | Most organisms (plants, animals, many microbes) | Yeast, some bacteria, parasites in the gut, **muscle during strenuous exercise**, flooded roots |

Any five clear differences gain full marks.
